placers.name: Melissa Gallo
placers.note: Class of 2031: a 7th grader in 2026 (3rd in 2025 as a 6th grader). Florida lets students below 9th grade wrestle for a member or feeder school, and these are real FHSAA medals — but the platform mints a profile only for a current class year (2027-2030), so a class of 2031 has nowhere to sit yet and a guessed one would be worse. The placement is stored and linked; she gets a profile when 2031 enters the window. Class year from the grade the tournament published, same source as every other Florida year (25 Oct 2026).

placers.name: Mason O'dell
placers.note: Class year held blank, so no profile. Flo's 2025 grade ('HS Freshman') and LarryBlustein's 2025 state preview ('27-10, Fr.') both read 2028; Kabra Wrestling's champion feature has him winning the 1A 106 title as an eighth grader in March 2023, which reads 2027. Flo's 2026 grade ('HS Senior') fits neither and looks like a data-entry error. No RankWrestlers record surfaced to break it. Held rather than guessed; detail in Muse's FL-grad-year-note.md (25 Oct 2026).

preFreshmanVerified.note: Zoe Delgado, Florida Christian School, class of 2029. She placed 8th in 2024 as a 7th grader and 2nd in 2025 as an 8th grader. Florida allows it: the FHSAA lets a student at a member or feeder school below 9th grade compete, and the bracket prints the grade, which is where the class year came from in the first place. Different from Maryland (COMAR 13A.06.03.02, grades 9-12 only) and Virginia (VHSL 28-2-1, eighth graders on junior varsity only), where the same shape proved a class year wrong (25 Oct 2026).
